meta.project: Integrated ESG-ABSA Intelligence Framework (v-1 to v3)
meta.description: Comprehensive reference mapping linking 5-layer integrated ESG research objectives to specific contributions, research questions, and validated empirical evidence from the 2025 literature corpus.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: AlignX: Advancing Multilingual Large Language Models with Multilingual Representation Alignment
literature_references.authors: Mengyu Bu, Yang Feng, ZhongJun He, Hua Wu, Shaolei Zhang
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C3 and RQ1.1 by providing a two-stage representation-level framework that aligns multilingual semantics to improve performance in non-dominant languages like Indonesian.

literature_references.title: Grounding Multilingual Multimodal LLMs With Cultural Knowledge
literature_references.authors: Simran Khanuja, Graham Neubig, Jean de Dieu Nyandwi, Yue-qi Song
literature_references.relevance: Justifies the regional calibration needs of RQ1.3 by demonstrating that grounding cultural knowledge in MLLMs narrows the performance gap in regional contexts.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?

literature_references.title: DCIS: Efficient Length Extrapolation of LLMs via Divide-and-Conquer Scaling Factor Search
literature_references.authors: Lei Yang, Shaoyang Xu, Deyi Xiong
literature_references.relevance: Provides the causal logic for C13 and RQ2.2 by introducing a divide-and-conquer search for scaling factors to extend context windows efficiently, addressing the scalability problems of long ESG documents.

literature_references.title: HookMoE: A learnable performance compensation strategy of Mixture-of-Experts for LLM inference acceleration
literature_references.authors: Along He, Mulin Li, Tao Li, Longkai Cheng, Xueshuo Xie
literature_references.relevance: Supports C10 and RQ2.4 by demonstrating a plug-and-play compensation framework that allows for efficient multi-model expert integration while maintaining task performance.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Direct Value Optimization: Improving Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs with Refined Values
literature_references.authors: Guangsheng Bao, Han Cui, Jun Wang, Linyi Yang, Yue Zhang, Hong-bo Zhang
literature_references.relevance: Supports C7 and RQ3.1 by utilizing value signals at individual reasoning steps to optimize CoT without intensive human annotation, aligning with neuro-symbolic objectives.

literature_references.title: Socratic-MCTS: Test-Time Visual Reasoning by Asking the Right Questions
literature_references.authors: David Acuna, Yejin Choi, Sanja Fidler, Jaehun Jung, Amlan Kar, Hyunwoo Kim, Ximing Lu
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the link for C4 and RQ3.2 by showing how sub-questioning and search can elicit hidden knowledge and produce extended reasoning traces.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.2: How can cross-model consistency be measured?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: The Stepwise Deception: Simulating the Evolution from True News to Fake News with LLM Agents
literature_references.authors: Yuhan Liu, Zirui Song, Xiaoqing Zhang, Xiuying Chen, Rui Yan
literature_references.relevance: Directly relevant to C11 and RQ4.5 by modeling how truthful information gradually distorts into misinformation, providing a parallel for detecting greenwashing in corporate narratives.

literature_references.title: reWordBench: Benchmarking and Improving the Robustness of Reward Models with Transformed Inputs
literature_references.authors: Asli Celikyilmaz, Andrew Cohen, Marjan Ghazvininejad, Yoon Kim, Zhaofeng Wu, Michihiro Yasunaga
literature_references.relevance: Supports C6 and RQ4.2 by analyzing the robustness of reward models to input transformations, which is critical for measuring cross-model consistency in risk assessment.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: CheckEval: A reliable LLM-as-a-Judge framework for evaluating text generation using checklists
literature_references.authors: Yukyung Lee, Joonghoon Kim, Jaehee Kim, Hyowon Cho, Jaewook Kang, Pilsung Kang, Najoung Kim
literature_references.relevance: Operationalizes RQ5.1 and C5 by providing a framework that decomposes criteria into traceable binary decisions for auditable, transparent outputs in production.

literature_references.title: Beyond A Single AI Cluster: A Survey of Decentralized LLM Training
literature_references.authors: Haotian Dong, Jingyan Jiang, Bowen Li, Rongwei Lu, Jia-jun Luo, Ying Shen, Jia-jun Song, Zhi Wang
literature_references.relevance: Supports C1 and RQ5.2 by evaluating decentralized resources and training, enabling the scalable deployment of large-scale models in resource-constrained environments.
